title: Corporate Governance: Principles, Policies and Best Practices
overview: Corporate governance has become an increasingly prominent topic in both academic and legislative circles, reflecting its critical role in modern business. While various governance models exist globally, they all aim to structure relationships between a company and its stakeholders. For instance, the Shareholder Wealth Maximization (SWM) model, prevalent in the US and UK, prioritizes shareholder rights, while models in Germany and Japan emphasize broader stakeholder involvement, such as employees and financiers.

This course delves into these governance models, explores single-tier and two-tier board structures, and examines the roles and responsibilities of board committees, including audit and remuneration committees. It also discusses the impact of institutional investors and the critical role of the chairman in governance.
audience: This course is designed for board members, senior executives, CFOs, directors, finance managers, legal advisors, corporate secretaries, auditors, HR managers, and department heads seeking to enhance their understanding of corporate governance principles and practices.
methodology: The program combines expert-led presentations with interactive exercises and case study discussions, encouraging participants to apply and analyze corporate governance principles in practical scenarios.
competencies: Structuring boards of directors and committees.
Assessing board powers and shareholder rights.
Maximizing corporate wealth while addressing stakeholder rights.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the core principles and importance of corporate governance.
Evaluate various governance models and propose enhancements.
Address ethical and policy considerations for stakeholders such as shareholders, boards of directors, auditors, and executives.
Determine the most suitable governance structure for a business model.
Implement best practices in corporate governance.
Apply disclosure and transparency standards in line with IFRS and other regulatory frameworks
